posts.title: Dotfiles That Save Themselves
posts.description: mise bootstrap already supported two common ways of managing dotfiles: keep them in a repository and symlink them into place, as GNU Stow does, or generate the live files from stored sources and templates, as chezmoi normally does. posts.title: Introducing packslip
posts.description: I’m introducing packslip , a signed manifest vendors publish alongside their releases. It tells package managers which binaries to download, how to verify and install them, and where to find matching shell completions and agent skills. mise supports packslip as a tier 1 backend, preferred over the github and aqua backends for new tools.
